subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Reference Points
description: A short lesson to help you apply Reference Points.

hook.text: A $50,000 salary feels great if you expected $40,000. It feels terrible if you expected $60,000. The money is the same.

buildup.text: Prospect theory says we evaluate outcomes relative to a reference point, not in absolute terms.

discovery.text: Anchoring sets reference points. A high initial price makes a discount feel generous. The anchor shapes perceived value.

twist.text: Olympic bronze medalists are happier than silver medalists. Silver compares to gold and feels like a loss.

climax.text: Happiness depends less on what you have and more on what you expected. Managing reference points manages satisfaction.

punchline.text: Same salary, different feelings. What you expected determines what you.

quiz.question: Why are bronze medalists often happier than silver medalists?
options: Silver medalists compare to gold (a loss) while bronze medalists compare to no medal (a gain)
